rationale: All 7 prior blocking findings (CR-001-CR-007 as supplied for this round) were verified against current source at HEAD and are resolved: the resolver now strips both dashed and concatenated release dates and ranks recency by an explicit non-vertex/date/lexicographic precedence, fetchTenantModelCatalog is decomposed under the 50-line standard with an AbortController timeout and a shared id/base_name/deployment_name fallback chain for both response shapes, the Claude Code JSONC writer now derives and applies the settings file's real formatting, and both previously-broken VS Code integration test files compile against the renamed VS_CODE_CAPABILITY_TABLE/VsCodeCapabilityEntry exports and the gatewayKey-required write signature. business_review and standards_review are carried forward unchanged from code-review-final.json since this check round does not re-run acceptance/standards audits (standards_path is null by contract on this round). No new findings were introduced; all 7 finding locations were present in changed_files and no fix_evidence was required since every finding is kind "code". Note: this round's supplied prior_verdict uses a 7-item CR-001-CR-007 numbering distinct from the 10-item numbering in the on-disk code-review-final.json, which also records two items outside this round's scope (a desktop.ts diagnostic-log gap and a malformed-proxyUrl TypeError) that this round did not verify.

findings.title: Date-stripping gap breaks single-number Claude family matching
findings.problem: RELEASE_DATE_PATTERN only matched separator-delimited dates (YYYY-MM-DD), so concatenated 8-digit dates (e.g. claude-opus-5-20260101) were never stripped before major/minor parsing.
findings.impact: For a single-number preferred family (e.g. claude-opus-5), the un-stripped date digits were read as the minor version instead of defaulting to 0, so a dated deployment of that family silently failed to identity-match and was dropped even though a serving deployment existed.
findings.recommendation: Widen RELEASE_DATE_PATTERN to also match a concatenated 8-digit date alternative, and strip it before major/minor extraction.

findings.title: pickMostRecent's lexicographic tie-break is unsound
findings.problem: pickMostRecent picked the same-identity candidate with the lexicographically largest raw string, which does not correspond to actual recency when candidates differ in shape (vendor-prefixed undated id vs. dashed dated id, or -vertex id vs. dated canonical id).
findings.impact: The wrong deployment could be silently selected for VS Code Copilot BYOK or Claude Desktop whenever a vertex id and a non-vertex id, or an undated and a dated id, coexisted for the same family.
findings.recommendation: Rank same-identity candidates by an explicit precedence: non-vertex over vertex, then parsed release date descending, then id text as a final deterministic tiebreak.

findings.title: fetchTenantModelCatalog violates the function-length/single-responsibility standard
findings.problem: fetchTenantModelCatalog combined the fetch call, HTTP status handling, content-type validation, response-shape parsing and three separate logging call sites in a single ~70-line function.
findings.impact: Violates code-quality.md's under-50-line/single-responsibility function standard for a function newly introduced by this change.
findings.recommendation: Extract the response-to-ids parsing and the logging calls into small named helpers, leaving fetchTenantModelCatalog as the top-level orchestration function.

findings.title: Tenant catalog fetch has no timeout/AbortController
findings.problem: The fetch(...) call inside fetchTenantModelCatalog carried no AbortController/timeout.
findings.impact: A hung or slow gateway would leave codemie proxy connect waiting indefinitely with no bound and no clear timeout error.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the fetch call in an AbortController with a bounded timeout, converting an AbortError into a clear, timeout-specific ConfigurationError.

findings.title: Tenant catalog's data-branch id extraction drops fallback fields
findings.problem: The array-shaped response branch resolved each id via id || base_name || deployment_name, but the { data: [...] } branch read only .id, ignoring the same fallback fields the module's own CodeMieLlmModel interface anticipates.
findings.impact: If the gateway ever returns a data-wrapped catalog whose entries use base_name/deployment_name instead of id, every such deployment id would be silently dropped, potentially failing the whole VS Code Copilot BYOK target with a false zero-match error.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same id || base_name || deployment_name fallback chain in the data-wrapped branch as the array branch already uses.

findings.title: VS Code Claude Code JSONC writes ignore the file's real formatting
findings.problem: Both modify() calls in writeVsCodeClaudeCodeConfigAtPath passed an empty {} as formattingOptions, which per jsonc-parser's contract inserts the edit completely unformatted (no newline, no indent) regardless of the file's existing style.
findings.impact: The two CodeMie-managed keys landed compact/unformatted in an otherwise hand-formatted settings.json, undermining this change's own comment/format-preservation intent.
findings.recommendation: Derive real formattingOptions (insertSpaces/tabSize/eol) from the existing file's raw text and pass them to both modify() calls.

findings.title: VS Code integration tests broken by connector API changes
findings.problem: tests/integration/vscode-byok.test.ts and tests/integration/vscode-models.live.test.ts imported the pre-rename VS_CODE_SUPPORTED_MODELS/VsCodeModelDefinition symbols and, in vscode-byok.test.ts's case, called writeVsCodeLanguageModelsConfigAtPath with only two arguments against a now three-argument (gatewayKey-required) signature.
findings.impact: Both files failed to compile against the renamed vscode-models.ts exports and the widened write-function signature, breaking the VS Code BYOK and live-certification integration suites.
findings.recommendation: Update both files' imports to VS_CODE_CAPABILITY_TABLE/VsCodeCapabilityEntry, use .family instead of .id, pass gatewayKey to the write call, and mock the tenant-catalog fetch endpoint.

finding_status.notes: RELEASE_DATE_PATTERN now matches concatenated 8-digit dates via extractReleaseDate; claude-opus-5 vs. claude-opus-5-20260101 now identity-matches (new resolver tests confirm).
pickMostRecent now ranks non-vertex-first, then parsed date descending, then lexicographic tiebreak; verified against new vertex-vs-dated and dashed-vs-undated cases.
fetchTenantModelCatalog decomposed into fetchWithTimeout/extractModelId/parseCatalogResponseIds/buildCatalogHttpError/log* helpers; body is now ~20 lines, single responsibility restored.
fetchWithTimeout wraps fetch in an AbortController with a 10s timeout; AbortError converts to a timeout-specific ConfigurationError; verified by new signal/timeout tests.
extractModelId's id/base_name/deployment_name fallback chain is now shared via parseCatalogResponseIds across both response shapes; verified by new data-wrapped fallback test.
detectFormattingOptions derives eol/indent/tabSize from the existing settings.json text and is passed to both modify() calls; verified by new tab- and space-indentation tests.

Both test files now import VS_CODE_CAPABILITY_TABLE/VsCodeCapabilityEntry and use .family; the write call passes gatewayKey and the mock serves /v1/llm_models. No stale references remain in src/tests.
